**[Section 8: Observations and Limitations]{.underline}**

**[8.1 Observations]{.underline}**

**Observation 1 --- Access Privileges.** Dr. Mehta was one of only six individuals within Pinnacle Dynamics Inc. who held full access privileges to the ZenithVault server. His access credentials (user account rmehta@pinnacledynamics.com) were valid and active throughout the entire exfiltration period and were not revoked until his formal departure from the company on May 9, 2025. While Dr. Mehta\'s system-level access to ZenithVault was authorized by virtue of his role as Chief Technology Officer, the bulk downloading of 4,217 files to a personal external USB storage device and the transmission of files to a personal email account exceeded any reasonable interpretation of authorized use of corporate systems and data.

**Observation 2 --- USB Device Not Recovered.** The SanDisk Extreme Pro USB 3.2 flash drive (Serial Number 04023A4D7F8B9C01) identified in the forensic examination is **not in Ironclad\'s possession** and was not among the company equipment surrendered by Dr. Mehta upon his departure from Pinnacle. Its current physical location and the integrity and completeness of its contents are unknown to Ironclad.

**Observation 3 --- Personal Gmail Account Beyond Investigative Reach.** The personal Gmail account (rajan.mehta.private@gmail.com) to which fourteen files were transmitted on April 22, 2025, is entirely beyond Ironclad\'s investigative reach. Ironclad cannot determine whether the files received at that account have been forwarded to additional recipients, downloaded to personal devices, shared via Google Drive or other cloud storage services, printed, or otherwise disseminated. The current status of those files is unknown, and Pinnacle has no unilateral means to ascertain their disposition.

**Observation 4 --- Correspondence with Vortech Automation Systems LLC.** During analysis of Dr. Mehta\'s corporate email account (the forensic image of the laptop includes locally cached email data via the Microsoft Outlook OST file), Ironclad observed that between **April 15 and April 24, 2025**, Dr. Mehta exchanged **seven emails** with an external email address: **fdoyle@vortechautomation.com**. **[Section 9: Conclusions]{.underline}**

Based on the forensic examination described in this report, Ironclad Digital Forensics LLC concludes, to a reasonable degree of forensic certainty, as follows:

> 1\. **USB Data Exfiltration.** Dr. Rajan Mehta transferred **4,217 files**, totaling approximately **3.8 GB** of data, from Pinnacle\'s ZenithVault secure R&D server to a personal SanDisk Extreme Pro USB 3.2 flash drive over **twelve separate sessions** between **April 10 and April 25, 2025**.
>
> 2\. **Categories of Exfiltrated Materials.** The transferred files comprise four categories of Pinnacle proprietary materials: (a) **1,847** Zenith adaptive-control algorithm source code files, (b) **923** Zenith controller board hardware schematic files, (c) **412** customer requirement specification files for Pinnacle\'s top fifteen client accounts, and (d) **1,035** strategic product roadmap documents for the 2025--2027 planning period.
>
> 3\. **Email Exfiltration to Personal Cloud Account.** On **April 22, 2025**, Dr. Mehta additionally transmitted **fourteen files** containing Zenith algorithm documentation via email from his Pinnacle corporate account to his personal Gmail account (**rajan.mehta.private@gmail.com**), creating a **separate and independently accessible copy** of core proprietary materials in a cloud-based environment entirely outside Pinnacle\'s control. This email transfer poses a distinct and heightened preservation and dissemination risk, as detailed in Finding 6.3 of this report.
>
> 4\. **Premeditated and Systematic Pattern.** The exfiltration activity commenced **fifteen days before** Dr. Mehta submitted his resignation on April 25, 2025, and was conducted systematically, predominantly during evening hours, in a volume and pattern dramatically inconsistent with Dr. Mehta\'s normal business use of the ZenithVault system. Average daily download volume increased twenty-two-fold during the exfiltration period compared to the preceding ninety-day baseline.
>
> 5\. **Unaccounted Data.** The USB device has **not been returned** to Pinnacle and is not in Ironclad\'s custody. The personal Gmail copies of the fourteen files remain unaccounted for. The current status, location, and disposition of all exfiltrated data remain **unknown** to both Pinnacle and Ironclad. This gap represents a continuing and unresolved risk to Pinnacle\'s proprietary information.
>
> 6\. **Vortech Communications During Exfiltration Period.** Ironclad identified seven email communications between Dr. Mehta\'s corporate account and an email address associated with Franklin Doyle, CEO of Vortech Automation Systems LLC, exchanged during the period of April 15--24, 2025 --- the same period during which the data exfiltration was actively occurring. The substance of these communications was not reviewed and is not within the scope of this engagement, but the existence of this correspondence during the exfiltration window may warrant further investigation by the client and its counsel.

**Recommendation.** Given the dual exfiltration vectors (physical USB device and cloud-based personal email) and the inability to verify the current disposition of the exfiltrated data through any means available to Pinnacle or Ironclad, Ironclad strongly recommends that any remediation or legal remedy address **both** vectors specifically and independently. > \(a\) **Physical return and verified destruction** of the USB device, including forensic verification that the device has been identified, imaged for evidentiary purposes, and securely wiped;

>
> \(c\) **A preservation order** covering all of Dr. Mehta\'s electronic devices, accounts, and cloud storage services pending resolution of the underlying dispute, to prevent further dissemination or destruction of evidence.

Physical return of the USB device alone, without addressing the cloud email vector, would leave a significant and uncontrolled copy of core proprietary materials in an environment where Pinnacle has no visibility, no access, and no ability to verify containment.

**[I. Purpose and Executive Summary]{.underline}**

This memorandum summarizes the competitive threat posed by the departure of Dr. Rajan Mehta, Pinnacle\'s former Chief Technology Officer, and his immediate hiring by Vortech Automation Systems LLC as Executive Vice President---Advanced Systems. This assessment has been prepared at your request to support Pinnacle\'s evaluation of legal remedies, and I understand that outside counsel at Hargrove, Tillman & Beck LLP has been retained as of May 19, 2025, to advise on enforcement options.

The core of the threat is straightforward: Mehta possessed unparalleled access to the proprietary technology underlying Project Zenith, our most significant R&D initiative in the company\'s history. He was one of only six individuals with full access to Zenith\'s core adaptive-algorithm source code and proprietary hardware schematics. His move to Vortech --- a direct competitor that is now publicly accelerating its own competing product, Project Helix --- poses an existential risk to Pinnacle\'s \$37.2 million R&D investment to date and a projected revenue stream of \$120 million over the first three years of commercialization.

This memo addresses: (a) Mehta\'s unique knowledge and role at Pinnacle, (b) the competitive overlap between Zenith and Helix, (c) the suspicious acceleration of Vortech\'s development timeline, (d) the financial impact on Pinnacle, and (e) the urgency of the situation. Every day of delay increases the risk that our trade secrets are being irreversibly integrated into a competitor\'s product. I urge that we act without delay.

**[II. Background: Dr. Mehta\'s Role and Access at Pinnacle]{.underline}**

Dr. Rajan Mehta joined Pinnacle on March 1, 2018, as Chief Technology Officer, executing both an Employment Agreement and an IP Assignment and Confidentiality Agreement on that date. Pinnacle employs approximately 2,100 people, with 340 in its R&D division. Mehta oversaw the entire R&D function and reported directly to me.

Project Zenith formally launched in January 2023. Mehta was designated as project lead from inception. Zenith is Pinnacle\'s next-generation adaptive robotic process controller --- the most significant R&D initiative in the company\'s fourteen-year history. Mehta was one of only six individuals granted full access to the Zenith core adaptive-control algorithm source code and proprietary hardware schematics stored on Pinnacle\'s secure R&D server, known internally as \"ZenithVault.\"

Mehta\'s qualifications are, in my assessment, irreplaceable. He holds a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from MIT and spent more than seven years leading Pinnacle\'s technology strategy. He was the architect of the adaptive-control algorithm that represents the core differentiating technology of Project Zenith. His knowledge of the algorithm\'s design, its optimization parameters, and its integration with Pinnacle\'s proprietary hardware cannot be replicated or reverse-engineered --- he personally directed the algorithm\'s development over the full twenty-eight months of the project.

Mehta submitted his resignation on April 25, 2025, citing \"personal reasons,\" with his last day being May 9, 2025. On April 28, 2025, Pinnacle\'s IT security team discovered that between April 10 and April 25, 2025, Mehta downloaded 4,217 files --- approximately 3.8 gigabytes --- from ZenithVault to a personal USB drive. The downloaded files comprise 1,847 source code files, 923 hardware schematics, 412 customer requirement specifications from Pinnacle\'s top fifteen accounts, and 1,035 strategic product roadmap documents. Additionally, Ironclad Digital Forensics LLC confirmed on May 16, 2025, that Mehta emailed fourteen files containing Zenith algorithm documentation to a personal Gmail account (rajan.mehta.private@gmail.com) on April 22, 2025.

Despite three separate demand letters sent by you on April 29, May 2, and May 7, 2025, Mehta has not returned any materials. The five-business-day return deadline under the IP Assignment Agreement lapsed on May 16, 2025. As of the date of this memorandum, Mehta retains unauthorized possession of Pinnacle\'s most sensitive trade secrets.

**[III. Competitive Landscape: Pinnacle vs. Vortech]{.underline}**

Pinnacle Dynamics Inc. is a Delaware C-corporation formed in 2011, headquartered in Austin, Texas, with fiscal year 2024 annual revenue of approximately \$485 million. Pinnacle designs and manufactures programmable logic controllers and robotic process automation systems for heavy manufacturing. Vortech Automation Systems LLC is a Texas LLC formed in 2016, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, with fiscal year 2024 annual revenue of approximately \$310 million. Vortech is a direct competitor in the industrial PLC market.

The two companies compete head-to-head for many of the same industrial customers across North America. Their product lines overlap substantially in the industrial automation, PLC, and robotic process automation segments --- precisely the categories covered by Mehta\'s non-competition covenant. Section 7(a) of the Employment Agreement restricts Mehta from working in \"industrial automation, programmable logic controllers, or robotic process automation\" across \"North America\" for twenty-four months following termination, through May 9, 2027.

Mehta\'s new role at Vortech --- EVP---Advanced Systems --- falls squarely within the scope of that covenant. According to Vortech\'s May 14, 2025 press release, authored by CEO Franklin Doyle, Mehta will lead Vortech\'s \"next-generation industrial control systems\" development. This is functionally identical to the work Mehta performed at Pinnacle.

From a business perspective, the non-compete\'s scope directly mirrors the competitive overlap between our two companies. The twenty-four-month duration aligns with the typical product development cycle in this industry --- Zenith\'s own development has been twenty-eight months. The geographic restriction to North America reflects the actual market in which Pinnacle and Vortech compete. We are not seeking to prevent Mehta from working in unrelated fields; the restriction is targeted to the specific industry and geographic market in which Mehta\'s knowledge of our trade secrets would be devastating to our competitive position. In my assessment, this scope is entirely reasonable given Mehta\'s C-suite role, his access to our most sensitive proprietary information, and the direct head-to-head competition between Pinnacle and Vortech.

**[IV. The Vortech Threat: Project Helix and the Suspicious Timeline Acceleration]{.underline}**

Vortech recently announced its own next-generation controller platform, Project Helix. Originally, Vortech\'s publicly communicated timeline was consistent with a launch around Q2 2026 --- roughly in line with Pinnacle\'s planned Q2 2026 commercial launch for Project Zenith. However, in connection with Mehta\'s hiring on May 14, 2025, Vortech publicly announced an accelerated launch target of Q4 2025 --- a full six months ahead of Pinnacle\'s Zenith launch and a dramatic acceleration from Vortech\'s prior timeline. The Vortech press release quotes CEO Franklin Doyle referencing Mehta\'s \"deep expertise in next-generation industrial control systems\" and Vortech\'s \"accelerated timeline\" for Project Helix.

The most logical explanation is that Vortech is leveraging Mehta\'s knowledge of Pinnacle\'s Zenith adaptive-control algorithm and architecture --- and potentially the actual proprietary files Mehta downloaded --- to shortcut its own development process.

If Vortech launches Helix in Q4 2025, it will reach the market approximately six months before Zenith, erasing Pinnacle\'s first-mover advantage --- the entire strategic rationale for Project Zenith. Each day that passes without action increases the risk that our proprietary technology is being integrated into Helix. Once disclosed and incorporated into a competitor\'s product, trade secret value is destroyed permanently and cannot be recovered through monetary damages.

I must also flag an additional, deeply concerning development. On May 15, 2025, one day after the Vortech announcement, we learned that two senior Project Zenith engineers --- Dr. Lena Petrov, Principal Hardware Engineer, and James Nakamura, Lead Software Architect --- were each contacted by a Vortech HR representative who mentioned Dr. Mehta by name and referenced \"an exciting new controller platform.\" This suggests that Vortech and Mehta are not only leveraging Mehta\'s technical knowledge but are actively attempting to recruit Pinnacle\'s Zenith team, which would compound the damage exponentially.

                r = p.add_run(part[2:-2]); r.bold = True
            elif part.startswith('*'):
                r = p.add_run(part[1:-1]); r.italic = True
            else:
                r = p.add_run(part)
            if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
        return p

# ---------------- I. INTRODUCTION ----------------
B.h1("I.  INTRODUCTION AND SUMMARY OF THE APPLICATION")
B.para("Pinnacle Dynamics Inc. submits this Application for Emergency Measures pursuant to Article 29(1) of the Rules and Article 1 of Appendix V against its former Chief Technology Officer, Dr. Rajan Mehta. Pinnacle requests urgent interim and conservatory measures that cannot await the constitution of the arbitral tribunal, to preserve the status quo, to prevent the further dissemination and use of Pinnacle’s trade secrets, and to preserve evidence pending determination of the underlying dispute.")
B.para("The facts that make this Application urgent are established by contemporaneous forensic evidence and by the Respondent’s own public statements:")
B.sub("(a)", "**Systematic exfiltration.** Between 10 and 25 April 2025, while still serving as Pinnacle’s CTO, Dr. Mehta copied **4,217 files (approximately 3.8 GB)** from Pinnacle’s restricted R&D server “ZenithVault” to a personal USB flash drive in **twelve separate sessions**, every one of which began on a weekday evening between 6:30 p.m. and 10:15 p.m. CDT. The files comprise the source code for Pinnacle’s Zenith adaptive-control algorithm (1,847 files), the Zenith controller-board hardware schematics (923 files), customer requirement specifications for Pinnacle’s top fifteen accounts (412 files), and Pinnacle’s 2025–2027 strategic product roadmap (1,035 files). Ironclad Report, §§ 5.1–5.2, 7, 9(1)–(2) (**C-3**).")
B.sub("(b)", "**A second, uncontainable channel.** On 22 April 2025 at 9:47 p.m. CDT, Dr. Mehta emailed fourteen core Zenith algorithm files (core source modules, design specifications, and test datasets) from his corporate account to his personal Gmail Account under the subject line “Reference Materials — Personal Backup.” Ironclad Report, §§ 6.1–6.3 (**C-3**).")
B.sub("(c)", "**Contemporaneous contact with a direct competitor.** Between 15 and 24 April 2025 — in the middle of the download campaign — Dr. Mehta exchanged seven emails with the CEO of Pinnacle’s principal competitor, Vortech, under subject lines including “Next steps” and “Re: Timing and logistics.” Ironclad Report, § 8.1, Observation 4 (**C-3**).")
B.sub("(d)", "**Resignation and immediate competitive employment.** Dr. Mehta resigned on 25 April 2025 — the date of the final download session — and his employment ended on 9 May 2025. Five days later, on 14 May 2025, Vortech announced his appointment as “Executive Vice President — Advanced Systems” to “oversee all aspects of Vortech’s advanced controller development operations” and to drive an “accelerated timeline” for Vortech’s competing adaptive-control controller platform, “Project Helix,” now targeted for commercial launch in **Q4 2025** — ahead of Zenith’s planned Q2 2026 launch (**C-5**; **C-7**).")
B.sub("(e)", "**Solicitation of the Zenith team.** Within 24 hours of that announcement, a Vortech recruiter contacted two of Pinnacle’s most senior Zenith engineers — Dr. Lena Petrov (Principal Hardware Engineer) and Mr. James Nakamura (Lead Software Architect) — stating that Dr. Mehta had “recommended” them and had “specifically mentioned [Mr. Nakamura’s] name” (**C-6**).")
B.sub("(f)", "**Refusal to return anything.** Despite three written demands (29 April, 2 May and 7 May 2025) and the expiry on 16 May 2025 of the contractual five-business-day return deadline under IPA § 4.1, Dr. Mehta has returned nothing, certified nothing, and identified no device or account. His only communication was a non-substantive acknowledgment of 30 April 2025 — sent, notably, from the very Gmail Account to which the Zenith files had been emailed (**C-4**).")
B.para("Dr. Mehta expressly agreed that any breach or threatened breach of his confidentiality, restrictive-covenant and intellectual-property obligations “would cause the Company immediate and irreparable harm” (EA § 9(a); IPA § 6.1), and that Pinnacle may seek emergency relief from an emergency arbitrator under the Rules (EA § 12(c); IPA §§ 9.2–9.3). In IPA § 9.3 he “specifically consent[ed] to the application of the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions and agree[d] not to challenge the authority of any emergency arbitrator.”")
B.para("Pinnacle seeks narrowly tailored measures, set out in full in Section VIII, that (i) freeze and preserve the evidence; (ii) prohibit any use or disclosure of the Zenith Materials; (iii) require delivery of the USB Device and all copies into the custody of an independent forensic examiner; (iv) require a sworn accounting of every device, account and person that has received the Zenith Materials; (v) provide for neutral forensic imaging and, thereafter, supervised remediation of the Respondent’s personal devices and accounts, including the Gmail Account; (vi) enjoin solicitation of Pinnacle employees and customers; and (vii) enforce the non-competition covenant pending the tribunal’s decision — or, in the alternative, at minimum bar Dr. Mehta from any work on Project Helix or any adaptive-control or programmable-controller development. Every measure tracks an obligation Dr. Mehta freely undertook.")
B.para("Without these measures, by the time a three-member tribunal is constituted (see ¶ 21 below) the Zenith Materials may be irreversibly embedded in a competing product scheduled to reach the market within months. Trade-secret value, once lost, cannot be restored by an award of damages.")

B.h1("II.  THE PARTIES AND THEIR REPRESENTATIVES")
B.h2("A.  The Applicant")
B.para("**Pinnacle Dynamics Inc.** is a corporation organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, U.S.A., with its principal offices at 4200 Innovation Parkway, Suite 300, Austin, Texas 78759, U.S.A. Pinnacle designs, develops, manufactures and sells programmable logic controllers (“PLCs”), robotic process automation systems and industrial automation solutions. B.para("Pinnacle is represented in these proceedings by **Hargrove, Tillman & Beck LLP**, [address], [telephone], [email] (Attention: [lead counsel]), to whom all communications should be addressed, with a copy to Mr. Marcus Engel, General Counsel, Pinnacle Dynamics Inc., 4200 Innovation Parkway, Suite 300, Austin, Texas 78759; telephone (512) 555-4100; email m.engel@pinnacledynamics.com. B.h2("B.  The Respondent")
B.para("**Dr. Rajan Mehta** is an individual residing at 1815 Cedar Ridge Lane, Austin, Texas 78746, U.S.A. B.para("Contact details for the Respondent: (i) the notice address and email designated in EA § 13(f), namely 1815 Cedar Ridge Lane, Austin, Texas 78746 and rajan.mehta@personal.net; and (ii) the email address rajan.mehta.private@gmail.com, which Dr. Mehta used to correspond with Pinnacle on 30 April 2025 (**C-4**). B.h2("C.  Non-Party: Vortech Automation Systems LLC")
B.para("Vortech is a Texas limited liability company headquartered in Dallas, Texas, with fiscal year 2024 revenue of approximately US$310 million, and is Pinnacle’s direct competitor in the industrial PLC market (**C-5**; **C-7**). B.h1("III.  THE ARBITRATION AGREEMENTS, JURISDICTION AND APPLICABILITY OF THE EMERGENCY ARBITRATOR PROVISIONS")
B.h2("A.  The arbitration agreements (Appendix V, Art. 1(3)(f))")
B.para("This Application is based on two arbitration agreements, both providing for ICC arbitration seated in New York:")
B.sub("(a)", "**EA § 12(a)** provides that “[a]ny dispute, claim, or controversy arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, enforcement, interpretation, or validity thereof … shall be resolved exclusively by final and binding arbitration administered by the International Court of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce … under the ICC Rules of Arbitration.” The seat is New York, New York; the language is English; the tribunal is a sole arbitrator unless the amount in controversy exceeds US$5,000,000, in which case three arbitrators. **EA § 12(c)** expressly preserves the right to “seek emergency or interim relief from an emergency arbitrator appointed pursuant to the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions of the ICC Rules,” and provides that “the emergency arbitrator provisions of the ICC Rules are incorporated into and form part of this agreement to arbitrate.”")
B.sub("(b)", "**IPA § 9.1** provides for final and binding ICC arbitration of “[a]ny dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement,” seated in New York, New York, in English, before a sole arbitrator unless the parties agree otherwise or the ICC Court determines that three arbitrators are warranted. **IPA § 9.2** authorizes either party to “apply to the ICC for the appointment of an emergency arbitrator pursuant to Article 29 of the ICC Rules and the ICC Emergency Arbitrator Provisions (Appendix V to the 2021 ICC Rules of Arbitration).” **IPA § 9.3** incorporates Appendix V by reference and records that the Employee “specifically consents to the application of the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions and agrees not to challenge the authority of any emergency arbitrator appointed under such provisions.”")
B.para("Both agreements were executed on 1 March 2018 by Pinnacle (through its CEO, Sandra Whitfield) and by Dr. Mehta personally, and are expressly to be “read in conjunction” with one another (EA §§ 8(e), 13(a); IPA preamble and § 8.3). Copies are submitted as **Exhibits C-1** and **C-2**.")
B.h2("B.  Prima facie jurisdiction of the Emergency Arbitrator and applicability of Appendix V")
B.para("The conditions of Article 29 are satisfied on a prima facie basis:")
B.sub("(a)", "**Article 29(5):** Both Pinnacle and Dr. Mehta are signatories of the arbitration agreements relied upon. No relief is sought against any non-signatory.")
B.sub("(b)", "**Article 29(6):** None of the exclusions applies. Both arbitration agreements were concluded on 1 March 2018, i.e., after 1 January 2012; the parties did not opt out of the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions — to the contrary, they expressly opted in (EA § 12(c); IPA §§ 9.2–9.3); the agreements are contractual, not treaty-based; and the parties agreed no other pre-arbitral procedure for interim measures. B.sub("(c)", "**Subject-matter scope:** The claims concern breach of EA §§ 5, 6(h), 7 and 8 and IPA §§ 2, 4 and 5, and related statutory and common-law claims, all of which “aris[e] out of or relat[e] to” the agreements. EA § 12(a) further delegates questions of “scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate” to the arbitrators.")
B.sub("(d)", "**Urgency requirement of Article 29(1):** addressed in Section VII.B below.")
B.para("**Version of the Rules.** EA § 12(a) refers to “the ICC Rules of Arbitration (2021 edition) then in effect,” and IPA § 9.1 to the Rules “in effect at the time of filing (currently the 2021 ICC Rules of Arbitration).” In any event, under Article 6(1) of the Rules the parties are deemed to have submitted to the Rules in effect on the date of commencement of the proceedings. The Rules in force as from 1 January 2021, including Appendix V, therefore govern.")
B.h2("C.  Agreements as to place, applicable law and language (Appendix V, Art. 1(3)(g))")

B.sub("(b)", "**A second, uncontainable channel.** On 22 April 2025 at 9:47 p.m. CDT, Dr. Mehta emailed fourteen core Zenith algorithm files (core source modules, design specifications, and test datasets) from his corporate account to his personal Gmail Account under the subject line \u201cReference Materials \u2014 Personal Backup.\u201d Ironclad Report, \u00a7\u00a7 6.1\u20136.3 (**C-3**).")

B.sub("(d)", "**Resignation and immediate competitive employment.** Dr. Mehta resigned on 25 April 2025 \u2014 the date of the final download session \u2014 and his employment ended on 9 May 2025. B.sub("(e)", "**Solicitation of the Zenith team.** Within 24 hours of that announcement, a Vortech recruiter contacted two of Pinnacle\u2019s most senior Zenith engineers \u2014 Dr. Lena Petrov (Principal Hardware Engineer) and Mr. James Nakamura (Lead Software Architect) \u2014 stating that Dr. Mehta had \u201crecommended\u201d them and had \u201cspecifically mentioned [Mr. Nakamura\u2019s] name\u201d (**C-6**).")

B.para("Project Zenith is Pinnacle’s next-generation adaptive robotic process controller and the most significant R&D initiative in the company’s history. B.para("Pinnacle’s Finance & Strategy Division records cumulative investment in Project Zenith from Q1 2023 through Q1 2025 of **US$37.2 million**, comprising personnel costs (US$14.6 million), prototyping (US$9.8 million), testing infrastructure (US$7.4 million), and licensing and IP acquisition (US$5.4 million) (**C-7**). Management’s three-year post-launch projections forecast Zenith revenue of approximately **US$120 million** (Year 1: US$35 million; Year 2: US$42 million; Year 3: US$43 million), on the express assumption that Pinnacle retains its estimated 18-month competitive lead derived from its proprietary adaptive-control algorithm and hardware design (**C-7**, Assumptions 4(a)).")

B.h2("D.  The Gmail exfiltration: 22 April 2025")
B.para("On 22 April 2025 at 9:47 p.m. CDT — approximately two and a half hours after that evening’s USB session began at 7:20 p.m. — Dr. Mehta emailed fourteen files (approximately 47 MB) from rmehta@pinnacledynamics.com to **rajan.mehta.private@gmail.com**, subject “Reference Materials — Personal Backup.” Delivery succeeded (Findings 6.1–6.2). B.para("This is a distinct and more dangerous vector. Data in a personal cloud email account persists on third-party servers, synchronizes to any device linked to the account, and can be forwarded or shared without any audit trail visible to Pinnacle (Finding 6.3(a)–(e)). B.para("Dr. Mehta controls the Gmail Account: he used it on 30 April 2025 to acknowledge Pinnacle’s first demand (**C-4**).")

B.para("The locally cached Outlook data on Dr. Mehta’s laptop shows that between 15 and 24 April 2025 he exchanged **seven emails** with fdoyle@vortechautomation.com, an address that appears to belong to Franklin Doyle, Vortech’s CEO, under subject lines including “Follow up — conversation,” “Next steps,” and “Re: Timing and logistics” (Ironclad Report, § 8.1, Observation 4; § 9(6)). B.para("Dr. Mehta tendered his resignation on 25 April 2025, citing “personal reasons”; his employment ended on Friday, 9 May 2025 (the “Termination Date”) following the fourteen-day notice period under EA § 6(c) (**C-4**; **C-8**).")

B.para("On **14 May 2025** — five days after the Termination Date and two days before the Return Deadline — Vortech issued a press release announcing Dr. Mehta’s appointment, “effective immediately,” as Executive Vice President — Advanced Systems, reporting directly to Mr. Doyle, to “oversee all aspects of Vortech’s advanced controller development operations” (**C-5**). B.h2("H.  Solicitation of the Zenith engineering team: 14–15 May 2025")
B.para("On **14 May 2025** at approximately 3:45 p.m. CDT — the day of the announcement — Ms. Rachel Inman, Talent Acquisition Manager at Vortech, telephoned Dr. Lena Petrov, Pinnacle’s Principal Hardware Engineer on the Zenith team and a former direct report of Dr. Mehta, on her personal mobile phone. B.para("As of the date of this Application: (i) the USB Device and the 4,217 files remain outside Pinnacle’s control; (ii) the fourteen emailed files remain in, or have been further propagated from, the Gmail Account; (iii) Dr. Mehta is directing Vortech’s advanced controller development for a product with a Q4 2025 launch target; (iv) Vortech is recruiting Pinnacle’s Zenith engineers by invoking Dr. Mehta’s personal recommendation; and (v) Dr. Mehta has refused to provide any assurance, accounting or certification. # ---------------- V. UNDERLYING DISPUTE ----------------
B.h1("V.  THE UNDERLYING DISPUTE TO BE REFERRED TO ARBITRATION")
B.para("In its Request for Arbitration, Pinnacle will assert, without limitation, the following claims against Dr. Mehta, each arising out of or relating to the Employment Agreement and/or the IP Agreement:")
B.sub("(a)", "breach of the confidentiality, non-use and no-personal-copy obligations (EA § 5; IPA §§ 2.1–2.3);")
B.sub("(b)", "breach of the return, destruction, certification and audit obligations (EA § 6(h); IPA §§ 4.1–4.5);")
B.sub("(c)", "breach of the non-competition covenant (EA § 7(a));")
B.sub("(d)", "breach and threatened breach of the employee and customer non-solicitation covenants (EA §§ 7(b)–(c); IPA §§ 5.1–5.2);")
B.sub("(e)", "misappropriation of trade secrets under the Defend Trade Secrets Act of 2016, 18 U.S.C. § 1836 *et seq.* (“DTSA”), and New York common law;")
B.sub("(f)", "breach of the fiduciary duty of loyalty owed by Dr. Mehta as a corporate officer during his employment, including through the April 2025 downloads and his concurrent dealings with Vortech; and")
B.sub("(g)", "declaratory relief (including tolling of the Restricted Period under EA § 7(f) and IPA § 6.3), permanent injunctive relief, damages and/or disgorgement in an amount to be quantified (presently expected materially to exceed US$5,000,000), and attorneys’ fees, expert fees and costs (EA § 12(d); IPA § 9.4).")
B.para("Nothing in this Application is intended to limit the claims Pinnacle may advance in its Request for Arbitration.")

# ---------------- VI. STANDARD ----------------
B.h1("VI.  THE APPLICABLE STANDARD FOR EMERGENCY MEASURES")
B.para("Article 29(1) of the Rules permits a party “that needs urgent interim or conservatory measures that cannot await the constitution of an arbitral tribunal” to apply for such measures. Article 28(1) authorizes “any interim or conservatory measure [the tribunal] deems appropriate,” and Article 6(7) of Appendix V permits the emergency arbitrator to make the Order “subject to such conditions as the emergency arbitrator thinks appropriate, including requiring the provision of appropriate security.” The parties also agreed that the arbitrator “shall have the authority to award any remedy or relief that would be available from a court,” including equitable relief (EA § 12(a); IPA § 9.1), and that emergency measures may be granted to “preserve the status quo, prevent irreparable harm, or protect or preserve the subject matter of the dispute” (EA § 12(c)).")
B.para("Neither the Rules nor Appendix V prescribes a substantive test. Emergency arbitrators acting under the Rules have consistently considered, as reflected in the ICC Commission Report on Emergency Arbitrator Proceedings (2019), whether the applicant has shown: (1) prima facie jurisdiction; (2) urgency, in the sense that the measures cannot await the constitution of the tribunal; (3) a risk of irreparable or serious harm not adequately reparable by damages; (4) a reasonable possibility of success on the merits (a prima facie case), without prejudging the merits; and (5) proportionality, i.e., that the balance of convenience favours the measures.")
B.para("These criteria are consistent with the law of the seat and the governing law. Under New York law, a preliminary injunction requires a likelihood of success on the merits, irreparable injury absent relief, and a balance of equities in the movant’s favour (*Doe v. Axelrod*, 73 N.Y.2d 748, 750 (1988)); and a New York court may grant provisional relief in aid of arbitration where the award “may be rendered ineffectual without such provisional relief” (N.Y. C.P.L.R. 7502(c)). The Second Circuit applies materially the same test in trade-secret and restrictive-covenant cases (*Faiveley Transport Malmo AB v. Wabtec Corp.*, 559 F.3d 110, 116 (2d Cir. 2009); *Ticor Title Ins. Co. v. Cohen*, 173 F.3d 63, 68–69 (2d Cir. 1999)). Pinnacle invokes these authorities as persuasive guidance; the Emergency Arbitrator is not bound by domestic procedural standards for court injunctions.")

# ---------------- VII. ARGUMENT ----------------
B.h1("VII.  THE APPLICANT SATISFIES EACH REQUIREMENT FOR EMERGENCY MEASURES")
B.h2("A.  Prima facie jurisdiction")
B.para("For the reasons in Section III, the Emergency Arbitrator has prima facie jurisdiction: the parties are signatories to two ICC arbitration agreements that expressly incorporate the Emergency Arbitrator Provisions, the dispute falls within their scope, and no Article 29(6) exclusion applies. Dr. Mehta has, moreover, contractually agreed “not to challenge the authority of any emergency arbitrator” (IPA § 9.3).")

B.h2("B.  Urgency: the measures cannot await the constitution of the arbitral tribunal")
B.para("The harm Pinnacle seeks to prevent is occurring now and will be complete long before a tribunal can act:")
B.sub("(a)", "**The data are uncontrolled and the cloud copy is propagating.** The USB Device and the Gmail Account are entirely outside Pinnacle’s visibility (Ironclad Report, Observations 2–3). Each day the Gmail copy persists, it may be synchronized to additional devices or forwarded without trace (Finding 6.3). Evidence of what Dr. Mehta has done with the materials — including access, forwarding and deletion logs — is equally at risk of loss.")
B.sub("(b)", "**Dr. Mehta is already leading a competitor’s controller development.** Since 14 May 2025 Dr. Mehta has overseen “all aspects” of Vortech’s advanced controller development, on an “accelerated timeline” for a Q4 2025 launch of an adaptive-control platform — i.e., within approximately four to seven months (**C-5**). Every week of work on Helix by the architect of Zenith, in possession of Zenith source code and schematics, increases the risk that Pinnacle’s trade secrets become irreversibly embedded in a competing product.")
B.sub("(c)", "**Solicitation is ongoing.** Vortech’s recruiter approached two key Zenith engineers within 24 hours of the announcement, invoking Dr. Mehta’s personal recommendation (**C-6**). There is every reason to expect further approaches to the remaining members of the Zenith team, each of whom carries Zenith know-how.")
B.sub("(d)", "**A tribunal cannot be constituted in time.** Pinnacle’s claims exceed US$5,000,000; under EA § 12(a) a three-member tribunal is required. The Request must be filed and notified, the Respondent has 30 days to answer and nominate (Articles 5 and 12 of the Rules), and confirmation, any challenge, and transmission of the file follow. Constitution of the tribunal will in all likelihood not occur before the second half of 2025, by which time Helix may be at or near launch.", )
B.para("Pinnacle has acted with diligence. It discovered the transfers on 28 April 2025, engaged forensic experts the same day, made three written demands within nine days, afforded Dr. Mehta the full contractual Return Deadline (16 May 2025), received Ironclad’s final report on 16 May 2025, retained outside counsel on 19 May 2025, and filed this Application immediately thereafter. Pinnacle’s measured approach — giving the Respondent every opportunity to comply voluntarily — cannot be held against it; the urgency arises from Dr. Mehta’s refusal and from Vortech’s 14 May announcement. *Cf. Citibank, N.A. v. Citytrust*, 756 F.2d 273, 276 (2d Cir. 1985) (unexplained delay may undercut irreparable harm; none exists here).", label="trib")

B.h2("C.  Pinnacle has a strong prima facie case on the merits")
B.h3("1.  Breach of the confidentiality and no-personal-copy obligations (EA § 5; IPA §§ 2.1–2.3)")
B.para("The Zenith Materials fall squarely within the contractual definitions of Confidential Information, which expressly include “source code, algorithms, hardware designs and schematics, … product roadmaps, customer lists, customer requirements and specifications” (EA § 1.6; IPA § 1.1(b), (c), (e), (f)). IPA § 2.3 flatly prohibits copying Confidential Information to “any personal device” or transmitting it to “any personal email address (including, without limitation, any personal Gmail … account)” absent written authorization of the General Counsel or CIO, and confirms that authorization to access materials on Company systems “does not constitute authorization to transfer, copy, or reproduce” them elsewhere. The forensic evidence establishes both prohibited acts (Findings 5.1–5.2, 6.1–6.2). No authorization was sought or given (**C-4**). The breach is established on the documents alone.")
B.h3("2.  Breach of the return, certification and audit obligations (EA § 6(h); IPA § 4)")
B.para("IPA § 4.1 required return of all Company Materials — including copies on personal devices and personal email accounts (IPA § 4.2(c)–(d)) — by 16 May 2025, and IPA § 4.3 required a certification under penalty of perjury identifying every device and account from which materials were deleted. The parties agreed that failure to meet the Return Deadline “shall constitute a material breach.” Dr. Mehta has done nothing. EA § 6(h) independently required return “at any time upon the Company’s request,” which Pinnacle made on 29 April 2025. Further, under IPA § 4.4 Dr. Mehta has already agreed to a forensic examination of “any personal device, personal account, or other medium” used to store Company Materials and to provide “all necessary access, passwords, credentials, and authorizations.” The forensic measures requested in Section VIII therefore do no more than give interim effect to an existing contractual right.")
B.h3("3.  Trade-secret misappropriation (DTSA; New York common law)")
B.para("The DTSA defines a trade secret as information that the owner has taken reasonable measures to keep secret and that derives independent economic value from not being generally known (18 U.S.C. § 1839(3)); “misappropriation” includes acquisition by “improper means” and disclosure or use in breach of a duty to maintain secrecy (§ 1839(5)–(6)). New York common law, which looks to the factors in Restatement of Torts § 757, cmt. b, is to the same effect (*Ashland Mgmt. Inc. v. Janien*, 82 N.Y.2d 395, 407 (1993)).")
B.para("On a prima facie basis, each element is met. The adaptive-control source code, the controller-board schematics, the customer specifications and the forward roadmap are the paradigm of protectable technical and commercial secrets; Pinnacle invested US$37.2 million in developing the Zenith technology (**C-7**); and Pinnacle protected it through a segregated server accessible in full to only six people, comprehensive confidentiality and no-personal-copy agreements, and IT monitoring that detected the transfers (Ironclad Report, Observation 1; IPA §§ 2.1–2.3). Copying those secrets to personal media in breach of an express contractual prohibition, followed by refusal to return them and immediate employment with a competitor developing a directly competing adaptive-control controller, establishes at least a prima facie case of acquisition by improper means and of threatened use or disclosure. The DTSA expressly authorizes injunctions against “actual or threatened misappropriation” (18 U.S.C. § 1836(b)(3)(A)).")
B.para("Pinnacle does not rely on any “inevitable disclosure” theory. The DTSA precludes an injunction that would “prevent a person from entering into an employment relationship” where conditions are based “merely on the information the person knows” (18 U.S.C. § 1836(b)(3)(A)(i)(I)), and New York courts treat inevitable-disclosure arguments with caution (*EarthWeb, Inc. v. Schlack*, 71 F. Supp. 2d 299, 310–11 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)). The trade-secret-based measures sought here rest on **documentary evidence of actual taking** of identified files, not on what Dr. Mehta carries in his head. The employment-related measure (Section VIII, Measure 8) rests on Dr. Mehta’s separate contractual non-competition covenant, not on the DTSA.")
B.h3("4.  Breach of the non-solicitation covenants (EA § 7(b); IPA § 5.1)")
B.para("EA § 7(b)(ii) prohibits Dr. Mehta from “assist[ing], encourag[ing], or facilitat[ing] any other person or entity in soliciting [or] recruiting” Pinnacle employees, and IPA § 5.1 provides that prohibited indirect solicitation “includes … directing or requesting that any third party (including … any recruiter, placement agency, or future employer) undertake any such solicitation.” Vortech’s recruiter told both Dr. Petrov and Mr. Nakamura that Dr. Mehta had personally identified and recommended them for Vortech’s controller platform (**C-6**). Identifying Pinnacle’s key Zenith engineers by name to Vortech’s talent-acquisition function so that Vortech could approach them is precisely the indirect solicitation that both covenants prohibit. That Dr. Mehta did not personally contact the engineers is immaterial under the express contractual language.")
B.para("Pinnacle acknowledges that the evidence of Dr. Mehta’s role consists of statements attributed to him by Vortech’s recruiter, recorded in contemporaneous HR reports and, for Mr. Nakamura, a preserved screenshot. That evidence is consistent, contemporaneous and corroborated by the timing; in any event, the standard at this stage is a reasonable possibility of success, and the Emergency Arbitrator is not bound by technical rules of evidence. The Respondent will have every opportunity to respond.")
B.h3("5.  Threatened breach of the customer non-solicitation covenants (EA § 7(c); IPA § 5.2)")
B.para("Dr. Mehta took 412 files of customer requirement specifications for Pinnacle’s fifteen largest accounts and is now leading the development of a competing product aimed at the same heavy-manufacturing customer base in North America (**C-3**; **C-5**; **C-7**, Assumption 1(c)). EA § 9(a) and IPA § 6.1 expressly extend equitable relief to “threatened breach.” Interim relief preventing solicitation of those customers, and use of their specifications, is warranted before a breach occurs rather than after the customer relationships have been diverted.")
B.h3("6.  Breach of the non-competition covenant (EA § 7(a))")
B.para("**Breach.** Vortech “designs, manufactures, and services programmable logic controllers and industrial automation platforms” (**C-5**) and is therefore a “Competing Business” (EA § 1.5). Dr. Mehta is employed by Vortech in Texas, within the Restricted Territory, within the 24-month Restricted Period running from 9 May 2025, in a role overseeing “all aspects” of advanced controller development — duties “the same as or substantially similar to” his role as Pinnacle’s CTO and Zenith project lead (EA §§ 2(a), 7(a)(i)). The breach is apparent on the face of Vortech’s own announcement.")
B.para("**Enforceability under New York law.** New York enforces a post-employment restraint to the extent it (1) is no greater than required to protect a legitimate interest of the employer, (2) does not impose undue hardship on the employee, and (3) is not injurious to the public (*BDO Seidman v. Hirshberg*, 93 N.Y.2d 382, 388–89 (1999)). Protection of trade secrets and confidential customer information, and against competitive use of an employee’s unique services, are recognized legitimate interests (*id.* at 389–92; *Reed, Roberts Assocs. v. Strauman*, 40 N.Y.2d 303, 308 (1976); *Ticor Title*, 173 F.3d at 70–72). Each factor is satisfied here on a prima facie basis:")
B.sub("(a)", "**Legitimate interest.** Dr. Mehta was one of six persons with full access to the Zenith crown jewels and the architect of the adaptive-control algorithm; he has in fact taken those materials (Section IV). This is the strongest form of the trade-secret interest New York protects.")
B.sub("(b)", "**Reasonable scope.** The covenant is confined by function — it reaches only roles involving duties substantially similar to his CTO duties or the use of Confidential Information (EA § 7(a)(i)) — and by industry (industrial automation, PLCs and robotic process automation). Its 24-month duration corresponds to the product-development cycle in this industry (Zenith itself has been in development for 28 months) and its North American territory corresponds to the market in which Pinnacle and Vortech actually compete (**C-8**, § III; EA § 7(d)(iii)).")
B.sub("(c)", "**No undue hardship.** Dr. Mehta, an MIT-trained electrical engineer, acknowledged that his skills extend beyond the restricted fields (EA § 7(d)(iv)), received substantial compensation in exchange for the covenant (EA §§ 4, 7(d)(vi)), and resigned voluntarily. Moreover, the interim measure Pinnacle primarily seeks is time-limited to the period before the tribunal can rule, and Pinnacle proposes an alternative narrower measure (Measure 8(b)).")
B.sub("(d)", "**No public injury.** Enforcing a negotiated covenant against a senior executive who has taken trade secrets serves, rather than injures, the public interest in commercial integrity.")
B.para("Even if any aspect of the covenant were considered overbroad, the parties expressly authorized the arbitrator to “modify, reform, or ‘blue pencil’” it and to enforce it “to the maximum extent permitted” (EA § 7(e)); New York permits partial enforcement where, as here, the employer has not engaged in overreaching and the employee was a senior executive who had the opportunity to consult counsel (*BDO Seidman*, 93 N.Y.2d at 394–95; EA §§ 7(d)(v), 14).")
B.para("**Choice of law.** Pinnacle anticipates that Dr. Mehta, a Texas resident employed in Texas, may contend that Texas law governs the covenant notwithstanding the parties’ New York choice of law (EA § 12(b)). That contention would not alter the prima facie analysis. Texas likewise enforces non-competition covenants that are ancillary to an otherwise enforceable agreement — including an employer’s provision of confidential information — and reasonable as to time, geography and scope of activity (Tex. Bus. & Com. Code §§ 15.50–15.52; *Marsh USA Inc. v. Cook*, 354 S.W.3d 764 (Tex. 2011)), and Texas courts must reform rather than void an overbroad covenant (§ 15.51(c)). The covenant here was given in exchange for access to Pinnacle’s most sensitive Confidential Information (EA Recitals; § 7(d)(ii)). In any event, the confidentiality, return, forensic-examination and non-solicitation measures sought do not depend on the non-competition covenant at all.")
B.h3("7.  Breach of fiduciary duty")
B.para("As Pinnacle’s CTO through 9 May 2025, Dr. Mehta owed Pinnacle a duty of undivided loyalty and was contractually bound to “act in the best interests of the Company at all times” (EA § 2(d)). Systematically copying Pinnacle’s core technology to personal media while corresponding with a competitor’s CEO about “next steps” and “timing and logistics” is, prima facie, a breach of that duty (*cf. Phansalkar v. Andersen Weinroth & Co.*, 344 F.3d 184, 200–02 (2d Cir. 2003) (faithless-servant doctrine)). This claim reinforces the prima facie case but is not necessary to any measure sought.")

B.h2("D.  Pinnacle faces imminent, irreparable harm that damages cannot remedy")
B.para("**Contractual acknowledgment.** Dr. Mehta agreed that breach or threatened breach of EA §§ 5, 7 and 8 “would cause the Company immediate and irreparable harm … for which monetary damages alone would be an inadequate and insufficient remedy” (EA § 9(a); IPA §§ 2.2, 6.1). While not conclusive, such an acknowledgment by a sophisticated executive who had the opportunity to consult counsel is entitled to substantial weight (*Ticor Title*, 173 F.3d at 69).")
B.para("**Loss of trade secrets.** “A trade secret once lost is, of course, lost forever,” and its loss “cannot be measured in money damages” (*FMC Corp. v. Taiwan Tainan Giant Indus. Co.*, 730 F.2d 61, 63 (2d Cir. 1984)). Irreparable harm is established where there is a danger that a misappropriator will disseminate the secrets more widely or otherwise irreparably impair their value (*Faiveley*, 559 F.3d at 118–19). Both dangers are present: the materials sit on an unaccounted-for USB device and in a personal cloud account susceptible to untraceable forwarding (Finding 6.3), and the person holding them now directs development of a competing product for a competitor that has publicly accelerated its launch. Once Zenith source code, schematics or customer specifications are incorporated into Helix or disclosed to Vortech personnel, no award can restore their secrecy.")
B.para("**Loss of first-mover advantage, customer goodwill and key personnel.** Pinnacle’s Zenith projections assume an 18-month competitive lead; management estimates that a competitor reaching the market first would reduce projected Zenith revenue by 50–70% in Year 1 and 30–50% in Years 2–3 (**C-7**, Assumption 4(b)) — on management’s percentages, a loss in the range of approximately US$43–67 million of the US$120 million projected. The harm extends beyond these figures to lost market position, the confidence of Pinnacle’s top fifteen customers whose specifications were taken, and the potential loss of the engineers on whom Zenith’s schedule depends (**C-7**, Assumption 5; **C-8**, § V). These consequences are inherently difficult to quantify and to reverse once the market has moved.")
B.para("**Inadequacy of damages.** Pinnacle’s CEO estimates Dr. Mehta’s personal net worth at approximately US$3.5 million (**C-8**, § V) — a fraction of Pinnacle’s exposure and of its US$37.2 million investment. A damages award against Dr. Mehta could not make Pinnacle whole.")

B.h2("E.  The balance of convenience and proportionality favour the measures")
B.para("The measures impose minimal legitimate burden on Dr. Mehta. He has no right to retain, use or disclose Pinnacle’s files; returning and accounting for them, preserving evidence, and submitting to a neutral examination to which he already consented (IPA § 4.4) costs him nothing he is entitled to keep. The non-solicitation measures merely require him to honour covenants he gave for consideration. The forensic protocol proposed in Measure 5 protects his personal and privileged information through a neutral examiner and search-term-based review. As to the non-competition measure, any hardship is self-inflicted: Dr. Mehta accepted the Vortech role knowing of the covenant, which Pinnacle had specifically reminded him of in writing (**C-4**, letters of 29 April and 7 May 2025); and Pinnacle proposes a narrower alternative (Measure 8(b)) that would permit him to remain employed while excluding him from the work in which the risk of misuse is greatest.")
B.para("By contrast, refusing the measures would expose Pinnacle to the permanent loss of its most valuable technology, the erosion of a US$37.2 million investment and a projected first-mover position, and the potential loss of key personnel — harm the Respondent’s own agreement characterizes as irreparable.")

B.h2("F.  The measures do not prejudge the merits")
B.para("The measures are conservatory: they preserve evidence, sequester the disputed materials with a neutral custodian rather than transferring them outright, maintain the contractual status quo ante, and are expressly subject to modification by the arbitral tribunal (Article 29(3) of the Rules; EA § 12(c); IPA § 9.2). Questions of liability, the full scope of misappropriation, damages and permanent relief are reserved for the tribunal.")

B.h2("G.  Security")
B.para("The parties agreed that equitable relief should be available “without the requirement of posting a bond, undertaking, or other security” unless mandatorily required (EA § 9(a)), and that any bond required should be “at the minimum amount permitted” (IPA § 6.1). Pinnacle — a company with annual revenue of approximately US$485 million — therefore requests that no security be required. Should the Emergency Arbitrator consider security appropriate under Article 6(7) of Appendix V (in particular in respect of Measure 8), Pinnacle offers an undertaking to compensate Dr. Mehta for any loss caused by the Order should the tribunal ultimately find it should not have been granted, or such modest security as the Emergency Arbitrator may fix.")

B.para("IPA \u00a7 4.1 required return of all Company Materials \u2014 including copies on personal devices and personal email accounts (IPA \u00a7 4.2(c)\u2013(d)) \u2014 by 16 May 2025, and IPA \u00a7 4.3 required a certification under penalty of perjury identifying every device and account from which materials were deleted. The parties agreed that failure to meet the Return Deadline \u201cshall constitute a material breach.\u201d Dr. Mehta has done nothing. EA \u00a7 6(h) independently required return \u201cat any time upon the Company\u2019s request,\u201d which Pinnacle made on 29 April 2025. Further, under IPA \u00a7 4.4 Dr. Mehta has already agreed to a forensic examination of \u201cany personal device, personal account, or other medium\u201d used to store Company Materials and to provide \u201call necessary access, passwords, credentials, and authorizations.\u201d The forensic measures requested in Section VIII therefore do no more than give interim effect to an existing contractual right.")
B.h3("3.  Trade-secret misappropriation (DTSA; New York common law)")
B.para("The DTSA defines a trade secret as information that the owner has taken reasonable measures to keep secret and that derives independent economic value from not being generally known (18 U.S.C. \u00a7 1839(3)); \u201cmisappropriation\u201d includes acquisition by \u201cimproper means\u201d and disclosure or use in breach of a duty to maintain secrecy (\u00a7 1839(5)\u2013(6)). New York common law, which looks to the factors in Restatement of Torts \u00a7 757, cmt. b, is to the same effect (*Ashland Mgmt. Inc. v. Janien*, 82 N.Y.2d 395, 407 (1993)).")
B.para("On a prima facie basis, each element is met. The adaptive-control source code, the controller-board schematics, the customer specifications and the forward roadmap are the paradigm of protectable technical and commercial secrets; Pinnacle invested US$37.2 million in developing the Zenith technology (**C-7**); and Pinnacle protected it through a segregated server accessible in full to only six people, comprehensive confidentiality and no-personal-copy agreements, and IT monitoring that detected the transfers (Ironclad Report, Observation 1; IPA \u00a7\u00a7 2.1\u20132.3). Copying those secrets to personal media in breach of an express contractual prohibition, followed by refusal to return them and immediate employment with a competitor developing a directly competing adaptive-control controller, establishes at least a prima facie case of acquisition by improper means and of threatened use or disclosure. The DTSA expressly authorizes injunctions against \u201cactual or threatened misappropriation\u201d (18 U.S.C. \u00a7 1836(b)(3)(A)).")
B.para("Pinnacle does not rely on any \u201cinevitable disclosure\u201d theory. The DTSA precludes an injunction that would \u201cprevent a person from entering into an employment relationship\u201d where conditions are based \u201cmerely on the information the person knows\u201d (18 U.S.C. \u00a7 1836(b)(3)(A)(i)(I)), and New York courts treat inevitable-disclosure arguments with caution (*EarthWeb, Inc. v. Schlack*, 71 F. Supp. 2d 299, 310\u201311 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)). The trade-secret-based measures sought here rest on **documentary evidence of actual taking** of identified files, not on what Dr. Mehta carries in his head. The employment-related measure (Section VIII, Measure 8) rests on Dr. Mehta\u2019s separate contractual non-competition covenant, not on the DTSA.")
B.h3("4.  Breach of the non-solicitation covenants (EA \u00a7 7(b); IPA \u00a7 5.1)")
B.para("EA \u00a7 7(b)(ii) prohibits Dr. Mehta from \u201cassist[ing], encourag[ing], or facilitat[ing] any other person or entity in soliciting [or] recruiting\u201d Pinnacle employees, and IPA \u00a7 5.1 provides that prohibited indirect solicitation \u201cincludes \u2026 directing or requesting that any third party (including \u2026 any recruiter, placement agency, or future employer) undertake any such solicitation.\u201d Vortech\u2019s recruiter told both Dr. Petrov and Mr. Nakamura that Dr. Mehta had personally identified and recommended them for Vortech\u2019s controller platform (**C-6**). Identifying Pinnacle\u2019s key Zenith engineers by name to Vortech\u2019s talent-acquisition function so that Vortech could approach them is precisely the indirect solicitation that both covenants prohibit. That Dr. Mehta did not personally contact the engineers is immaterial under the express contractual language.")
B.para("Pinnacle acknowledges that the evidence of Dr. Mehta\u2019s role consists of statements attributed to him by Vortech\u2019s recruiter, recorded in contemporaneous HR reports and, for Mr. Nakamura, a preserved screenshot. That evidence is consistent, contemporaneous and corroborated by the timing; in any event, the standard at this stage is a reasonable possibility of success, and the Emergency Arbitrator is not bound by technical rules of evidence. The Respondent will have every opportunity to respond.")
B.h3("5.  Threatened breach of the customer non-solicitation covenants (EA \u00a7 7(c); IPA \u00a7 5.2)")
B.para("Dr. Mehta took 412 files of customer requirement specifications for Pinnacle\u2019s fifteen largest accounts and is now leading the development of a competing product aimed at the same heavy-manufacturing customer base in North America (**C-3**; **C-5**; **C-7**, Assumption 1(c)). EA \u00a7 9(a) and IPA \u00a7 6.1 expressly extend equitable relief to \u201cthreatened breach.\u201d Interim relief preventing solicitation of those customers, and use of their specifications, is warranted before a breach occurs rather than after the customer relationships have been diverted.")
B.h3("6.  Breach of the non-competition covenant (EA \u00a7 7(a))")
B.para("**Breach.** Vortech \u201cdesigns, manufactures, and services programmable logic controllers and industrial automation platforms\u201d (**C-5**) and is therefore a \u201cCompeting Business\u201d (EA \u00a7 1.5). Dr. Mehta is employed by Vortech in Texas, within the Restricted Territory, within the 24-month Restricted Period running from 9 May 2025, in a role overseeing \u201call aspects\u201d of advanced controller development \u2014 duties \u201cthe same as or substantially similar to\u201d his role as Pinnacle\u2019s CTO and Zenith project lead (EA \u00a7\u00a7 2(a), 7(a)(i)). The breach is apparent on the face of Vortech\u2019s own announcement.")
B.para("**Enforceability under New York law.** New York enforces a post-employment restraint to the extent it (1) is no greater than required to protect a legitimate interest of the employer, (2) does not impose undue hardship on the employee, and (3) is not injurious to the public (*BDO Seidman v. Hirshberg*, 93 N.Y.2d 382, 388\u201389 (1999)). Protection of trade secrets and confidential customer information, and against competitive use of an employee\u2019s unique services, are recognized legitimate interests (*id.* at 389\u201392; *Reed, Roberts Assocs. v. Strauman*, 40 N.Y.2d 303, 308 (1976); *Ticor Title*, 173 F.3d at 70\u201372). Each factor is satisfied here on a prima facie basis:")
B.sub("(a)", "**Legitimate interest.** Dr. Mehta was one of six persons with full access to the Zenith crown jewels and the architect of the adaptive-control algorithm; he has in fact taken those materials (Section IV). This is the strongest form of the trade-secret interest New York protects.")
B.sub("(b)", "**Reasonable scope.** The covenant is confined by function \u2014 it reaches only roles involving duties substantially similar to his CTO duties or the use of Confidential Information (EA \u00a7 7(a)(i)) \u2014 and by industry (industrial automation, PLCs and robotic process automation). Its 24-month duration corresponds to the product-development cycle in this industry (Zenith itself has been in development for 28 months) and its North American territory corresponds to the market in which Pinnacle and Vortech actually compete (**C-8**, \u00a7 III; EA \u00a7 7(d)(iii)).")
B.sub("(c)", "**No undue hardship.** Dr. Mehta, an MIT-trained electrical engineer, acknowledged that his skills extend beyond the restricted fields (EA \u00a7 7(d)(iv)), received substantial compensation in exchange for the covenant (EA \u00a7\u00a7 4, 7(d)(vi)), and resigned voluntarily. Moreover, the interim measure Pinnacle primarily seeks is time-limited to the period before the tribunal can rule, and Pinnacle proposes an alternative narrower measure (Measure 8(b)).")
B.sub("(d)", "**No public injury.** Enforcing a negotiated covenant against a senior executive who has taken trade secrets serves, rather than injures, the public interest in commercial integrity.")
B.para("Even if any aspect of the covenant were considered overbroad, the parties expressly authorized the arbitrator to \u201cmodify, reform, or \u2018blue pencil\u2019\u201d it and to enforce it \u201cto the maximum extent permitted\u201d (EA \u00a7 7(e)); New York permits partial enforcement where, as here, the employer has not engaged in overreaching and the employee was a senior executive who had the opportunity to consult counsel (*BDO Seidman*, 93 N.Y.2d at 394\u201395; EA \u00a7\u00a7 7(d)(v), 14).")
B.para("**Choice of law.** Pinnacle anticipates that Dr. Mehta, a Texas resident employed in Texas, may contend that Texas law governs the covenant notwithstanding the parties\u2019 New York choice of law (EA \u00a7 12(b)). That contention would not alter the prima facie analysis. Texas likewise enforces non-competition covenants that are ancillary to an otherwise enforceable agreement \u2014 including an employer\u2019s provision of confidential information \u2014 and reasonable as to time, geography and scope of activity (Tex. Bus. & Com. Code \u00a7\u00a7 15.50\u201315.52; *Marsh USA Inc. v. Cook*, 354 S.W.3d 764 (Tex. 2011)), and Texas courts must reform rather than void an overbroad covenant (\u00a7 15.51(c)). The covenant here was given in exchange for access to Pinnacle\u2019s most sensitive Confidential Information (EA Recitals; \u00a7 7(d)(ii)). In any event, the confidentiality, return, forensic-examination and non-solicitation measures sought do not depend on the non-competition covenant at all.")
B.h3("7.  Breach of fiduciary duty")
B.para("As Pinnacle\u2019s CTO through 9 May 2025, Dr. Mehta owed Pinnacle a duty of undivided loyalty and was contractually bound to \u201cact in the best interests of the Company at all times\u201d (EA \u00a7 2(d)). Systematically copying Pinnacle\u2019s core technology to personal media while corresponding with a competitor\u2019s CEO about \u201cnext steps\u201d and \u201ctiming and logistics\u201d is, prima facie, a breach of that duty (*cf. Phansalkar v. Andersen Weinroth & Co.*, 344 F.3d 184, 200\u201302 (2d Cir. 2003) (faithless-servant doctrine)). This claim reinforces the prima facie case but is not necessary to any measure sought.")

B.h2("D.  Pinnacle faces imminent, irreparable harm that damages cannot remedy")
B.para("**Contractual acknowledgment.** Dr. Mehta agreed that breach or threatened breach of EA \u00a7\u00a7 5, 7 and 8 \u201cwould cause the Company immediate and irreparable harm \u2026 for which monetary damages alone would be an inadequate and insufficient remedy\u201d (EA \u00a7 9(a); IPA \u00a7\u00a7 2.2, 6.1). While not conclusive, such an acknowledgment by a sophisticated executive who had the opportunity to consult counsel is entitled to substantial weight (*Ticor Title*, 173 F.3d at 69).")
B.para("**Loss of trade secrets.** \u201cA trade secret once lost is, of course, lost forever,\u201d and its loss \u201ccannot be measured in money damages\u201d (*FMC Corp. v. Taiwan Tainan Giant Indus. Co.*, 730 F.2d 61, 63 (2d Cir. 1984)). Irreparable harm is established where there is a danger that a misappropriator will disseminate the secrets more widely or otherwise irreparably impair their value (*Faiveley*, 559 F.3d at 118\u201319). Both dangers are present: the materials sit on an unaccounted-for USB device and in a personal cloud account susceptible to untraceable forwarding (Finding 6.3), and the person holding them now directs development of a competing product for a competitor that has publicly accelerated its launch. Once Zenith source code, schematics or customer specifications are incorporated into Helix or disclosed to Vortech personnel, no award can restore their secrecy.")
B.para("**Loss of first-mover advantage, customer goodwill and key personnel.** Pinnacle\u2019s Zenith projections assume an 18-month competitive lead; management estimates that a competitor reaching the market first would reduce projected Zenith revenue by 50\u201370% in Year 1 and 30\u201350% in Years 2\u20133 (**C-7**, Assumption 4(b)) \u2014 on management\u2019s percentages, a loss in the range of approximately US$43\u201367 million of the US$120 million projected. The harm extends beyond these figures to lost market position, the confidence of Pinnacle\u2019s top fifteen customers whose specifications were taken, and the potential loss of the engineers on whom Zenith\u2019s schedule depends (**C-7**, Assumption 5; **C-8**, \u00a7 V). These consequences are inherently difficult to quantify and to reverse once the market has moved.")
B.para("**Inadequacy of damages.** Pinnacle\u2019s CEO estimates Dr. Mehta\u2019s personal net worth at approximately US$3.5 million (**C-8**, \u00a7 V) \u2014 a fraction of Pinnacle\u2019s exposure and of its US$37.2 million investment. A damages award against Dr. Mehta could not make Pinnacle whole.")

B.h2("E.  The balance of convenience and proportionality favour the measures")
B.para("The measures impose minimal legitimate burden on Dr. Mehta. He has no right to retain, use or disclose Pinnacle\u2019s files; returning and accounting for them, preserving evidence, and submitting to a neutral examination to which he already consented (IPA \u00a7 4.4) costs him nothing he is entitled to keep. The non-solicitation measures merely require him to honour covenants he gave for consideration. The forensic protocol proposed in Measure 5 protects his personal and privileged information through a neutral examiner and search-term-based review. As to the non-competition measure, any hardship is self-inflicted: Dr. Mehta accepted the Vortech role knowing of the covenant, which Pinnacle had specifically reminded him of in writing (**C-4**, letters of 29 April and 7 May 2025); and Pinnacle proposes a narrower alternative (Measure 8(b)) that would permit him to remain employed while excluding him from the work in which the risk of misuse is greatest.")
B.para("By contrast, refusing the measures would expose Pinnacle to the permanent loss of its most valuable technology, the erosion of a US$37.2 million investment and a projected first-mover position, and the potential loss of key personnel \u2014 harm the Respondent\u2019s own agreement characterizes as irreparable.")

B.h2("F.  The measures do not prejudge the merits")
B.para("The measures are conservatory: they preserve evidence, sequester the disputed materials with a neutral custodian rather than transferring them outright, maintain the contractual status quo ante, and are expressly subject to modification by the arbitral tribunal (Article 29(3) of the Rules; EA \u00a7 12(c); IPA \u00a7 9.2). Questions of liability, the full scope of misappropriation, damages and permanent relief are reserved for the tribunal.")

B.h2("G.  Security")
B.para("The parties agreed that equitable relief should be available \u201cwithout the requirement of posting a bond, undertaking, or other security\u201d unless mandatorily required (EA \u00a7 9(a)), and that any bond required should be \u201cat the minimum amount permitted\u201d (IPA \u00a7 6.1). Pinnacle \u2014 a company with annual revenue of approximately US$485 million \u2014 therefore requests that no security be required. Should the Emergency Arbitrator consider security appropriate under Article 6(7) of Appendix V (in particular in respect of Measure 8), Pinnacle offers an undertaking to compensate Dr. Mehta for any loss caused by the Order should the tribunal ultimately find it should not have been granted, or such modest security as the Emergency Arbitrator may fix.")
EOF
