/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh /home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/arbitration-international-dispute-resolution/draft-emergency-arbitrator-application/claude-code-session/20261015-111520 'cat > /workspace/part5.py <<"EOF"
# ---------------- VIII. MEASURES ----------------
B.h1("VIII.  EMERGENCY MEASURES REQUESTED")
B.para("For the reasons set out above, Pinnacle respectfully requests that the Emergency Arbitrator issue an Order pursuant to Article 29 of the Rules and Article 6 of Appendix V in the following terms (the “Measures”). For purposes of the Measures, “Pinnacle Confidential Information” has the meaning of “Confidential Information” in EA § 1.6 and IPA § 1.1, and includes the Zenith Materials; “the Neutral” means an independent digital forensic examiner, unaffiliated with either party, agreed by the parties within three (3) business days of the Order or, failing agreement, designated by the Emergency Arbitrator from candidates proposed by the parties, whose fees shall be advanced by Pinnacle (consistent with IPA § 4.4) subject to the tribunal’s final allocation of costs.")
B.sub("Measure 1", "**Preservation.** Dr. Mehta shall, with immediate effect, preserve and shall not delete, destroy, wipe, overwrite, alter, conceal, transfer or dispose of (a) the USB Device; (b) any other storage device, computer, tablet or mobile phone in his possession, custody or control on which any Pinnacle Confidential Information is or has been stored since 10 April 2025; (c) the Gmail Account and any other email, messaging or cloud-storage account to which any Pinnacle Confidential Information has been sent, uploaded or synchronized, including all associated access, forwarding, sharing, download and deletion logs; and (d) all communications between Dr. Mehta and any director, officer, employee or agent of Vortech from 1 January 2025 to date. Dr. Mehta shall not deactivate, close or change the recovery settings of any such account.", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 2", "**Non-use and non-disclosure.** Dr. Mehta shall not, directly or indirectly, access, use, copy, disclose, transmit, publish or make available any Pinnacle Confidential Information to any person or entity, including Vortech and any of its directors, officers, employees, contractors or agents, for any purpose other than compliance with the Order.", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 3", "**Delivery into neutral custody.** Within two (2) business days of the Order, Dr. Mehta shall deliver to the Neutral (a) the USB Device; (b) every other physical medium containing any of the Zenith Materials or other Pinnacle Confidential Information; and (c) all hard-copy documents containing or derived from Pinnacle Confidential Information. The Neutral shall hold all such items in secure custody, forensically image them, and make no disclosure of their contents except as provided in Measure 5 or by further order.", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 4", "**Sworn accounting.** Within three (3) business days of the Order, Dr. Mehta shall serve a declaration signed under penalty of perjury (consistent with IPA § 4.3) that: (a) identifies by make, model and serial number or account name every device, storage medium, email account, cloud-storage account and messaging account on which any Pinnacle Confidential Information has been stored, received or accessed since 10 April 2025; (b) states the present location of the USB Device and of every copy of the Zenith Materials, in whole or in part; (c) identifies every person or entity (including any Vortech personnel) to whom any Pinnacle Confidential Information has been disclosed, transmitted, shown or described since 10 April 2025, with the date, manner and content of each disclosure; (d) states whether any of the fourteen files emailed to the Gmail Account on 22 April 2025 has been forwarded, downloaded, shared or uploaded, and if so to or by whom; (e) identifies any deletion, wiping or destruction of any Pinnacle Confidential Information or any relevant device or account since 10 April 2025; and (f) identifies any Pinnacle employee whose name, contact details or qualifications Dr. Mehta has provided to Vortech or any recruiter since 10 April 2025.", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 5", "**Neutral forensic imaging and supervised remediation.** (a) Within five (5) business days of the Order, Dr. Mehta shall make available to the Neutral every device and account identified (or required to be identified) under Measure 4, together with the Gmail Account, and shall provide all passwords, credentials, multi-factor authentication and consents necessary for the Neutral to create forensic images or complete exports of them (as contemplated by IPA § 4.4). (b) The Neutral shall search the images and exports using the SHA-256 hash values identified in the Ironclad Report, the ZenithVault file inventory to be supplied by Pinnacle, and reasonable search terms agreed between the parties or fixed by the Emergency Arbitrator, and shall report to both parties’ counsel (on an outside-counsel’s-eyes-only basis) the existence, location, access history and onward transmission of any responsive material, without disclosing Dr. Mehta’s unrelated personal or privileged information. (c) Upon delivery of the Neutral’s report, and with the forensic images retained by the Neutral pending the final award, the Neutral shall permanently remove all Pinnacle Confidential Information from those devices and accounts (including trash, deleted-items and backup locations) and shall certify completion of the remediation to the parties and the arbitral tribunal.", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 6", "**Non-solicitation of employees.** Dr. Mehta shall not, directly or indirectly (including through Vortech, any recruiter or any other third party), solicit, recruit, induce or encourage any person who is, or within the preceding six months was, an employee, contractor or consultant of Pinnacle to leave Pinnacle or to join Vortech or any other entity, and shall not identify, recommend, refer or provide information about any such person to Vortech or any recruiter for that purpose (EA § 7(b); IPA § 5.1).", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 7", "**Non-solicitation of customers.** Dr. Mehta shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, divert or attempt to divert the business of any customer or prospective customer of Pinnacle with whom he had material contact or about whom he obtained Confidential Information during the last two years of his employment — including the fifteen accounts whose specifications are contained in /ZenithVault/Client_Specs/ — for the purpose of providing competing products or services (EA § 7(c); IPA § 5.2).", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 8", "**Non-competition.** (a) Dr. Mehta shall refrain from being employed by, consulting for or rendering services to Vortech or any other Competing Business (EA § 1.5) within North America in any role involving duties the same as or substantially similar to those he performed as Pinnacle’s Chief Technology Officer, or involving the use or application of Pinnacle Confidential Information (EA § 7(a)), until the arbitral tribunal rules on this measure; **or, in the alternative,** (b) Dr. Mehta shall not, pending the arbitral tribunal’s determination, participate in any capacity in Project Helix or in the research, design, development, testing or commercialization of any adaptive-control algorithm, programmable logic controller, industrial controller hardware, firmware or related product roadmap for Vortech or any other Competing Business, and shall confirm his compliance by declaration under penalty of perjury every thirty (30) days.", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 9", "**Certification of compliance.** Within seven (7) business days of the Order, Dr. Mehta shall serve a declaration under penalty of perjury confirming his compliance with Measures 1 through 8, and shall notify Pinnacle’s counsel in writing within forty-eight (48) hours of discovering any further Pinnacle Confidential Information in his possession, custody or control (IPA § 4.5).", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 10", "**Duration.** The Order shall remain in effect until modified, terminated or superseded by the arbitral tribunal or by further order of the Emergency Arbitrator (Article 29(3) of the Rules; Article 6(6) and (8) of Appendix V; EA § 12(c)).", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 11", "**Costs.** Pursuant to Article 7(3) of Appendix V, the costs of these emergency arbitrator proceedings, including Pinnacle’s reasonable legal fees and expert costs, shall be borne by Dr. Mehta (EA § 12(d); IPA § 9.4), or, alternatively, their allocation shall be reserved to the arbitral tribunal (Article 29(4) of the Rules).", indent=1.3)
B.sub("Measure 12", "**Further relief.** Such further or other measures as the Emergency Arbitrator considers appropriate to preserve the status quo, protect Pinnacle Confidential Information and preserve evidence.", indent=1.3)

# ---------------- IX. PROCEDURAL ----------------
B.h1("IX.  PROCEDURAL REQUESTS")
B.para("Pinnacle respectfully requests that the Emergency Arbitrator:")
B.sub("(a)", "establish an expedited procedural timetable pursuant to Article 5(1) of Appendix V, providing for a written response by the Respondent within three (3) business days and a hearing by videoconference within seven (7) days of the transmission of the file, with the Order to be issued well within the 15-day period in Article 6(4) of Appendix V;")
B.sub("(b)", "pending the hearing, issue an immediate procedural direction requiring both parties to preserve all documents, devices and accounts relevant to this Application (corresponding to Measure 1), which Pinnacle submits is a procedural measure that causes the Respondent no prejudice and protects the integrity of the proceedings;")
B.sub("(c)", "direct that this Application, its exhibits and the Order be treated as confidential in accordance with EA § 12(e) and IPA § 9.5, and that the Zenith file descriptions in the exhibits be accessible only to the parties’ counsel, the Emergency Arbitrator and the Secretariat; and")
B.sub("(d)", "permit Pinnacle to supplement this Application with witness statements of Mr. Marcus Engel, Ms. Sandra Whitfield and Ms. Karen Liddell, and an expert declaration of Ms. Karen Stillwell (CFCE, EnCE) adopting the Ironclad Report, each of whom will be available for examination at the hearing.")
B.para("Pinnacle is transmitting a copy of this Application and its exhibits to the Respondent concurrently with its filing, by email to rajan.mehta.private@gmail.com and rajan.mehta@personal.net and by overnight courier to 1815 Cedar Ridge Lane, Austin, Texas 78746, consistent with EA § 13(f) and IPA § 8.7. Pinnacle does not seek any measure without notice to the Respondent.", label="serve")

I've drafted the ICC Article 29 emergency arbitrator application for Pinnacle Dynamics Inc. against Dr. Rajan Mehta. The file passes the docx skill's validate.py check and was parsed back successfully (about 12,500 words). It is drafted as a filing dated "[21] May 2025", in line with the documents, and still has placeholders for counsel details, the neutral examiner candidates, the power of attorney, proof of the US$40,000 fee payment, the LinkedIn screenshot and the signature.

I read all eight documents in full: both agreements, the Ironclad forensic report, the demand letters, the Vortech press release, the HR reports, the CEO memo and the financial spreadsheet.

**What the application covers**
- **Jurisdiction:** The application relies on two arbitration clauses: section 12 of the Employment Agreement and sections 9.1–9.3 of the IP Agreement. In section 9.3 Mehta agreed not to challenge an emergency arbitrator's authority. It shows that Articles 29(5) and 29(6) are satisfied, and it addresses the clause conflict on the number of arbitrators. It also commits Pinnacle to file the Request for Arbitration within 10 days, as Appendix V requires.
- **Facts:** All facts are cited to the exhibits. Mehta copied 4,217 files (3.8 GB) to a USB drive over 12 weekday-evening sessions, and emailed 14 files to his personal Gmail. He exchanged seven emails with Vortech's CEO while the copying was going on. He sent no substantive reply to three demand letters, and the contractual return deadline passed on 16 May 2025. Vortech hired him on 14 May to accelerate its competing product (Project Helix) to a Q4 2025 launch, and its recruiter then approached two of Pinnacle's Project Zenith engineers.
- **Legal test and argument:** The application applies the usual emergency arbitrator test, with New York and federal case law as persuasive support. It expressly does not rely on an "inevitable disclosure" theory, because federal trade secret law (the DTSA) would not support an injunction that blocks employment. It anticipates a Texas choice-of-law challenge to the non-compete and addresses security.
- **Relief:** It asks for 12 precise measures. These cover preservation of evidence and a ban on using or disclosing the files. Mehta would hand the USB drive to a neutral examiner, give a sworn accounting, and allow neutral imaging of his devices and the Gmail account before supervised deletion. They also cover no solicitation of employees or customers, and the non-compete with a narrower fallback that would only bar him from working on Project Helix.
- **Schedules and annex:** There is an exhibit index, a chronology, and a checklist against each item Appendix V, Article 1(3) requires. A final annex of internal drafting notes is marked to be removed before filing.

**Problems in the source documents (listed in the annex)**
- **Privilege:** The forensic report, HR reports and CEO memo are all marked privileged, so filing them waives privilege. I recommend replacing the CEO memo with a witness statement from the CEO, because it contains overstatements the other side would use against us.
- **Financial figures:** The spreadsheet's own loss percentages produce a loss of about $43–67M, not the $54–78M it states. The CEO memo's claim of losing "the full $120M" also conflicts with the spreadsheet. In Years 2–3, units times price do not equal the revenue shown; for example, Q2 2027 works out to $13.5M against $9.0M listed. The application uses only the $43–67M range calculated from management's percentages. The $37.2M investment figures do reconcile.
- **Forensic report:**
  - It mentions weekend downloads, but all 12 sessions were on weekdays.
  - Its logs stop on 28 April, while Mehta's access continued until 9 May. That gap should be pulled and analysed urgently.
  - The folder paths for the emailed files don't match the source-code folder they are said to come from.
  - No one has reviewed the content of the seven emails with Vortech's CEO. Those emails are on Pinnacle's own system and should be reviewed now.
- **Demand letters:** They cite the wrong sections (section 8 for confidentiality, which is section 5; section 7(b) for customers, which is 7(c); section 12(c) for fees, which is 12(d)). They also miscount the days since the earlier demands. The letters and the IP Agreement refer to a "New York Uniform Trade Secrets Act", which does not exist; New York protects trade secrets under common law. The application cites everything correctly.
- **Limits of the emergency arbitrator:** It cannot bind Vortech or Google, and Google cannot release email contents to a private party without the account holder's consent. The annex recommends considering parallel court relief, including ex parte DTSA seizure of the USB drive.
